acceptanceCriteria: The test records a load-aware guard or a calibrated relative budget, with the decision retained in a build-log entry, and a merge-queue run on a contended runner no longer fails on this test alone.
body:
Suspected flake (timing budget on a shared runner), not a confirmed regression.

Reproduction: merge-queue run 38376972938 for PR beamfall/corvint#854 (queue branch gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-854-d72617c46b4f..., 2026-10-13T09:31Z), job go-product-shard (7). measure_test.go:71 logged `incremental select over 390 units: n=160 p50=91.4ms p95=102.0ms max=105.8ms widest-plan=191 units`; measure_test.go:74 then failed `incremental select p95=102.042587ms exceeds the 100ms budget` (cold graph build 8.76s). The same tree passed go-product-shard (7) on the PR branch run (CI claude/v1-1278-s3-retire-packets, 09:09Z) and the PR touches no Go source under internal/liveverify (it retires packets and docs). Re-queued at 11:08Z (run 38388116872).

Expected: a performance budget test either runs under a load guard (skip or widen when the runner is contended, as the tasks-store timing tests in V1-1324 propose) or measures a ratio against a calibrated baseline on the same host, so a 2% miss on a shared runner does not evict a merge-queue entry.
Actual: a hard 100ms p95 budget measured on whatever runner the shard lands on; the margin is p50 91ms, so ordinary contention crosses it.

Version: origin/main d72617c46 + PR #854 head 5fcbf06bb. Related: V1-1324 (tasks-store timing tests under load).
title: internal/liveverify/affected: TestIncrementalSelectionMeetsTheLiveBudget fails on a loaded CI runner (p95 102ms vs 100ms budget)
